raw_response:
I am getting old, so this year I will still do it the steady way, not chase anything fancy. I only finished primary school, so I mostly look at what worked on my own land and what the neighbors do. Wheat and maize are still my main safe pair because they feed the house and bring cash. Cotton can still make money if the weather is decent, but it takes more watching and more picking, so I will not put too much land into it. Millet, mung bean, and peanut I keep on smaller pieces. They spread the risk, use different times of labor, and if one crop is not good, maybe another one carries us through. We only have two people at home, and well water costs money, so I will irrigate the wheat and cotton first, maize only if it turns dry, and the smaller crops mostly depend on rain unless they really suffer.

For fertilizer, I will not cut too hard because under-fertilizing hurts yield badly, but I also cannot waste money. Wheat gets the most careful feeding because if wheat stands well, the summer maize on that ground also starts better. Maize I will put base fertilizer and then one topdress if the rain comes right. Cotton I keep moderate, because too much fertilizer makes it grow rank and costs extra. Millet and mung bean I keep light. Peanut needs some base fertilizer, but not as heavy as wheat. I will do simple tillage, use local or commonly bought seed, and follow the local calendar like usual.
